message.content:
sorry lol, here it is

Where the Entire CLI puts its files
Local state is scattered across the working tree and eleven ad-hoc entries in the git directory. This proposes two roots, five lifecycle buckets, and one rule for deciding where anything new goes.

Repo entireio/cli
Status Proposal — one decision open
Date 2026-08-28
01
Goals
Two things, stated plainly, because everything below is judged against them.

Local files live outside the working tree. Nothing the CLI writes at runtime should appear in git status, be reachable by git clean -xdf, or need an ignore rule to stay invisible.
A structure, not a list. A contributor adding a new file should be able to derive its path from a rule, and a reviewer should be able to tell whether it is safe to delete without reading the code.
02
Current state
Every path the CLI writes today, split by whether git tracks it and by which checkouts can see it.

committed to the repo
local, shared by all worktrees
local, this worktree only
problem
Working tree
.entire/
.entire/settings.json            # committed
.entire/runners/                 # committed
.entire/redactors/               # committed
.entire/.gitignore               # committed

.entire/settings.local.json      # ignored
.entire/metadata/<sessionID>/    # ignored
.entire/logs/entire.log          # ignored
.entire/tmp/                     # ignored
.entire/redactors/local/          # ignored

.entire/worktrees/               # untracked, often unignored
Git directory
11 top-level entries
entire/preferences.json
entire/trail-refresh-spawn       (+ .lock)
entire/session-sweep-spawn       (+ .lock)
entire-sessions/
entire-session-locks/
entire-shadow-locks/
entire-investigations/<runID>/
entire-review/manifests/
entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl (+ .lock)
entire-redact-cache/
entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json (+ .lock)

All resolved against `git rev-parse
--git-common-dir`, never `.git`.
.entire/worktrees/ holds trail worktree checkouts (trail_checkout_worktree.go:26). ensureTrailWorktreeIgnoreRule appends its rule to the root .gitignore, and only if one already exists — so in a repo without a root .gitignore the checkouts are both untracked and unignored.

entire-sessions/ also carries per-session sidecars (.trail-scope.json, .model, .warn-stale-ended). Two orphan refs, entire/checkpoints/v1 and entire/trails/v1, are out of scope throughout.

Root resolution is already centralized: gitdir, entiredir, and worktreedir own the handles to the three trees. What is not centralized is the names — the eleven entries above are declared as constants in seven packages.

03
What's wrong
Four problems. None of them is fixed by renaming the entries.

Local files in the working tree are hostile to git
git clean -xdf deletes .entire/metadata/<sessionID>/ — the copied transcript and prompt.txt for every session in flight (lifecycle.go:748-813) — along with entire.log and tmp/. A routine cleanup silently destroys unfinished checkpoint work and the log that would explain it. Everything under a git directory is immune by construction.

Scattered paths leave nothing to secure
The eleven entries are declared as constants in seven packages — session/state.go:28, strategy/session_state.go:838, strategy/checkpoint_sync_capture.go:23, checkpoint/shadow_ref.go:139, checkpoint/pushqueue.go:26, checkpoint/redact_cache.go:72, investigate/state.go:25, review/manifest.go:759. Each package joins its own path onto a git root, so each has to defend that path itself.

It shows. The same session-ID traversal guard is written out seven times across three packages (session/state.go:952,997,1053, strategy/session_state.go:886, checkpoint/ephemeral.go:68,287, checkpoint/persistent.go:73) because there is no single owner of the join to put it in — and the names being guarded come from agent-supplied session IDs, tool-use IDs, and investigation run IDs, feeding directories that get RemoveAll'd.

The deeper cost is that there is no directory whose contents are all ours. entire-sessions/ is a sibling of HEAD, config, and hooks/, so nothing can be scoped to Entire's files as a unit: not a containment root, not a permission mode, not an audit, not a single RemoveAll. A bucket layout gives one root per tree and makes the bucket the only join, which is what containment can actually be anchored on.

Scattering also drifts silently. entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl is already declared in two places — checkpoint/pushqueue.go:26 and integration_test/multi_pushurl.go:31 — so renaming it in one leaves the other pointing at a file that no longer exists.

The scoping axis is invisible
All eleven git-directory entries resolve against the git common dir, so every linked worktree shares them — and review/marker_fallback.go:42 depends on exactly that. Nothing in the paths says so. Writing the target as .git/entire/… erases the distinction and is literally wrong inside a linked worktree, where .git is a file. The bug seed is already in the tree: strategy/common.go:356 defines gitDir = ".git" as a plain string.

.entire/metadata/ means two different things
paths.EntireMetadataDir is both an on-disk staging directory and a path inside the orphan-branch tree, read through go-git in manual_commit_hooks.go:1816,2817,2871, manual_commit_condensation.go:1444, and ephemeral.go:367. The in-tree layout is committed history on entire/checkpoints/v1.

Any move must split this constant first. Otherwise a rename to .git/entire/metadata changes the on-disk path and the tree path together, and the tool stops finding its own history.

04
Target layout
Two roots, chosen by whether a second worktree needs to see the file. Five buckets, chosen by lifecycle.

Working tree — committed content only
tracked
.entire/
├── settings.json            project settings
├── runners/*.json           trail runner configs
└── redactors/*.yaml         shared redaction packs

Deleted: .gitignore — nothing left to ignore.
Relocated: worktrees/ — destination open, see §08.
git rev-parse --git-common-dir
shared by every worktree
<git-common-dir>/entire/
├── config/                              user-authored, must survive
│   ├── preferences.json
│   ├── settings.local.json               ← from .entire/
│   ├── checkpoint-sync-remotes.json
│   └── redactors/local/                  ← from .entire/
├── state/                               derived but not reproducible
│   ├── sessions/<sessionID>.json
│   │             <sessionID>.trail-scope.json
│   ├── investigations/<runID>/
│   ├── review/manifests/
│   └── checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl
├── cache/                               rebuilt on demand
│   └── redact-cache/
└── run/                                  process-scoped, dead on reboot
    ├── session-locks/<sessionID>.lock
    ├── shadow-locks/<branch>.lock
    ├── checkpoint-push-queue.lock
    ├── checkpoint-sync-remotes.lock
    ├── trail-refresh-spawn              (+ .lock)
    └── session-sweep-spawn              (+ .lock)
git rev-parse --git-dir
this worktree only
<git-dir>/entire/
├── logs/entire.log                       ← from .entire/
├── metadata/<sessionID>/                 ← from .entire/ (on-disk staging only)
└── tmp/                                  ← from .entire/
Why these three are per-worktree
All three are scoped to one checkout by their content, and merging them would be a regression. Two agents in two worktrees interleave into one entire.log, making it unreadable exactly when you need it. metadata/<sessionID>/ stages the transcript for the checkpoint of this checkout's HEAD. tmp/ already collides on fixed names such as the pi hook cache (agent/pi/lifecycle.go:285).

redactors/local/ is config/, not cache/ — it is user-authored, not derived, and deleting it loses work.

05
Tradeoffs
What each change buys, and what it costs. None of the costs are blocking; two of them need a decision baked in from the start.

Moving local state out of the working tree
Everything the CLI writes at runtime leaves .entire/ for a git directory.

Gains
git clean -xdf can no longer destroy in-flight session data or the log that would explain the loss.
.entire/ becomes purely committed content, so "is this directory fully tracked?" is a one-line test assertion and .entire/.gitignore disappears.
Nothing the CLI does shows up in git status, so it can't be accidentally staged or land in a PR diff.
Costs
Paths get harder for a human to find by hand, especially in a linked worktree where the git dir is .git/worktrees/<name>/. Bug-report collection has to go through entire doctor bundle rather than a known path.
git clean stops resetting CLI state, so a user reaching for it to "start fresh" no longer gets that. entire clean becomes the only route.
Any external tooling or muscle memory pointing at .entire/logs breaks.
Two roots instead of one
Common dir for anything shared between worktrees; git dir for anything scoped to one checkout.

Gains
Makes the sharing axis explicit, and correct inside linked worktrees and submodules — where the single-root shorthand is simply wrong.
Retires the gitDir = ".git" string literal, the seed of the class of bug this fixes.
Fixes two live defects at once: interleaved logs from concurrent agents, and fixed-name collisions under tmp/.
Costs
Every new file needs a scoping decision, and a wrong one fails silently — a shared file placed per-worktree only misbehaves once someone adds a second worktree.
Two places to look when debugging, and migration has to handle both.
Five lifecycle buckets
config, state, cache, run, plus logs and tmp on the per-worktree side.

Gains
entire clean collapses from a hand-maintained path list into three RemoveAll calls that can't fall behind the code.
"Is this safe to delete?" is answerable from the path alone, by a reviewer who has not read the package.
A new file has a derivable home, so the layout stops accreting names.
Costs
Some files are genuinely ambiguous. checkpoint-sync-remotes.json is captured rather than authored, and sits in config/ only because losing it changes behaviour.
Locks move away from the data they guard, so a stale .lock is no longer next to the file it belongs to.
One more path segment everywhere.
One package owns every path, enforced by test
The name of every local file moves behind a typed accessor; a test forbids filepath.Join onto a git root anywhere else.

Gains
The layout cannot drift back. This is the only part of the proposal that is self-enforcing.
One place to validate an agent-supplied ID before it becomes a path, replacing the guard currently repeated across seven call sites.
Migration and the legacy-path fallback live in exactly one place, so they can be added and later removed cleanly.
Test helpers stop hardcoding .git/entire-sessions.
Costs
Seven feature packages gain a dependency on one path package — real coupling, in exchange for the guarantee.
The forbidding test needs an allowlist, and will occasionally block someone doing something legitimate.
Staged migration with a one-release fallback
Relocate once on first command of the new version, under a flock; read the legacy path for one minor release.

Gains
An upgrade landing mid-session doesn't lose state or strand a running agent's hooks.
Each of the four steps ships on its own, so a problem is bisectable to one release.
entire doctor can report leftovers instead of leaving them to rot.
Costs
Two path resolutions coexist for a release, which is exactly the ambiguity this proposal removes — so the fallback has to be deleted on schedule, not left in.
A rename across filesystems is not atomic and needs a copy fallback for the large redact-cache.
Downgrading to the previous version leaves the moved state unreadable.
06
The rules
This is the part that has to survive. Each one is testable.

R1
Everything under .entire/ is committed.
No code path writes there at runtime.
Makes .entire/.gitignore dead weight, and makes the directory's tracked state a one-line assertion in a test.
R2
Every local path is <root>/entire/<bucket>/…
root ∈ {git-common-dir, git-dir}, bucket ∈ {config, state, cache, run, logs, tmp}.
No file sits directly under entire/. No third naming shape.
R3
Root is chosen by one question: does a second worktree need to see this?
Yes → common dir. No → git dir.
Both come from git rev-parse, never from joining .git onto the worktree root. That is what makes the layout correct in linked worktrees and submodules.
R4
cache/, run/, and tmp/ are deletable at any moment, by anyone, including mid-session.
config/ and state/ are not.
Turns entire clean from a hand-maintained path list into three RemoveAll calls, and gives a reviewer a one-glance answer to "is this safe to nuke?"
R5
One package owns every join onto a git directory.
Nothing outside it calls filepath.Join(commonDir, …) or filepath.Join(gitDir, …).
Enforced by a test, not a convention. Without this, R2 decays back to the current state within a few features. The root handles are already centralized in gitdir/entiredir/worktreedir; this extends that to the names.
R6
On-disk paths and in-tree paths are separate constants.
The checkpoint branch keeps .entire/metadata/<sessionID>/ as its tree layout forever.
Prerequisite for the metadata move. Can land on its own, before anything else here.
07
Path-by-path
Every path the CLI writes, and where it lands. <common> and <git> abbreviate the two rev-parse roots.

Today    Target    Scope    Life    Note
Working tree — stays put
.entire/settings.json    unchanged    tracked    —    Project settings.
.entire/runners/    unchanged    tracked    —    Trail runner configs.
.entire/redactors/*.yaml    unchanged    tracked    —    Shared packs. local/ splits off.
.entire/.gitignore    deleted    —    —    Nothing left to ignore once R1 holds.
.entire/worktrees/    open — §08    —    —    Only remaining R1 violation.
Working tree → git directory
.entire/settings.local.json    <common>/entire/config/settings.local.json    shared    config    User-editable; needs a path command and doc updates.
.entire/redactors/local/    <common>/entire/config/redactors/local/    shared    config    LoadPacks must take two roots and merge.
.entire/logs/entire.log    <git>/entire/logs/entire.log    worktree    logs    Per-checkout so concurrent agents don't interleave.
.entire/metadata/<id>/    <git>/entire/metadata/<id>/    worktree    state    On-disk only. Tree path is frozen — R6.
.entire/tmp/    <git>/entire/tmp/    worktree    tmp    Fixed subpaths collide across worktrees today.
Git directory — regrouped
entire/preferences.json    <common>/entire/config/preferences.json    shared    config    Already in the right root.
entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json    <common>/entire/config/checkpoint-sync-remotes.json    shared    config    Captured remotes; not reproducible.
entire-sessions/    <common>/entire/state/sessions/    shared    state    Includes .trail-scope.json, .model, .warn-stale-ended.
entire-investigations/<runID>/    <common>/entire/state/investigations/<runID>/    shared    state    User-visible in an error string — update it.
entire-review/manifests/    <common>/entire/state/review/manifests/    shared    state    —
entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl    <common>/entire/state/checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl    shared    state    Losing it drops unpushed checkpoints.
entire-redact-cache/    <common>/entire/cache/redact-cache/    shared    cache    Already documented as safe to delete.
entire-session-locks/    <common>/entire/run/session-locks/    shared    run    —
entire-shadow-locks/    <common>/entire/run/shadow-locks/    shared    run    —
entire-*.lock    <common>/entire/run/*.lock    shared    run    Locks leave their data's directory.
entire/trail-refresh-spawn    <common>/entire/run/trail-refresh-spawn    shared    run    Throttle marker.
entire/session-sweep-spawn    <common>/entire/run/session-sweep-spawn    shared    run    Throttle marker.
08
The open decision
Where do trail worktree checkouts go?

.entire/worktrees/ is the last thing standing between this proposal and R1, and it is the largest object in the working tree — full source checkouts, not metadata. It should leave its current location and stay out of the git common dir, so all three candidates move real checkouts somewhere a person can comfortably cd into.

A. Sibling of the repo — ../<repo>.worktrees/<branch>/
Gains
Satisfies both constraints with no new machinery.
Checkouts stay one cd .. away, matching what people already do by hand.
Same filesystem as the repo, so checkout stays fast.
Costs
The CLI writes outside the repo it was invoked in — needs care around permissions.
Two clones of the same repo sharing a parent directory collide.
Cleanup on git worktree remove has to reach outside the repo too.
B. User state directory — ~/.local/state/entire/worktrees/<repo-id>/<branch>/
Gains
Cleanest separation: nothing near the repo at all.
Extends the tier that already exists in internal/entireclient/userdirs (~/.config/entire, ~/.cache/entire).
Costs
Paths become unguessable, so it needs an entire trail path command to be usable at all.
Needs a stable <repo-id> that survives the repo being moved — otherwise it orphans checkouts.
Often lands on a different filesystem from the repo: slow, and it breaks hardlink-based checkout optimizations.
C. Configurable, defaulting to A
Gains
Costs the least in surprise: the default is A's familiar location.
Lets a monorepo point every checkout at one scratch volume.
Costs
One more setting in .entire/settings.json to document and support.
Needs a validation path that rejects any location inside the working tree, or it reintroduces the problem it was added to solve.
Recommendation
Start at A and add C only if someone asks. B's filesystem-boundary risk is real for large repos, and the <repo-id> stability problem is a genuine source of orphaned checkouts. Whichever wins, the decision is independent of the rest of this proposal and should not block it.

09
Getting there
Order
Four steps, each independently shippable, in this order because each removes a hazard from the next.

Split the metadata constant (R6). Pure refactor, no path changes, no migration. Removes the trap.
Move the eleven names behind typed accessors (R5) that still return today's paths, and add the test that forbids joins elsewhere. The root handles already exist; this is about the names. No behaviour change.
Move the git-directory entries into buckets. Contained: nothing outside the accessor package changes.
Move the working-tree entries out, delete .entire/.gitignore, add the .entire-is-fully-tracked assertion.
Migration mechanics
The hazard is a CLI upgrade landing mid-session: an agent is running, hooks are firing, and the session state file moves underneath it. Relocate once, on first command of the new version, under a flock in the common dir — the same mechanism recentlySpawnedMarker already uses — so concurrent hooks serialize rather than racing. Rename directories rather than copying, so it is atomic within a filesystem and cheap for a large redact-cache.

Keep a read-only fallback to the legacy path for one minor release, so a session that started under the old binary and continues under the new one still resolves. Do not write to the legacy path. Drop the fallback on the following release, and have entire doctor report any legacy path still present.

Also needs updating
doctor_bundle.go:110 collects settings.local.json from .entire/.
clean.go enumerates paths by name — becomes three RemoveAll calls under R4.
redact.LoadPacks walks one directory recursively and finds local/ as a subdirectory; it needs two roots and a merge, and the local/ special case disappears.
User-facing strings naming these paths: remote_topology.go:178, the --local/--project flag help in setup.go, investigate/cmd.go:527, clean.go:26-30, doctor_logs.go.
Test helpers that hardcode .git/entire-sessions: integration_test/hooks.go:497,596,618, e2e/testutil/assertions.go:302, benchutil/benchutil.go:256.
Out of scope, stated so nobody moves them
In-tree checkpoint layout. .entire/metadata/<sessionID>/ on entire/checkpoints/v1 is committed history and stays exactly as it is.
Refs. entire/checkpoints/v1 and entire/trails/v1 are unaffected.
User-global directories. ~/.config/entire and ~/.cache/entire are a separate tier and already well-formed.
Git's own files. .git/hooks/ and the transient state files (rebase-merge, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, …) are git's, not ours.

7ac91dd4fb 2026-08-28 Peyton Montei
fix(settings): per-block strictness for the user settings file

LoadUserSettings strict-decoded the WHOLE file, so a newer entire adding any

Verified both. Short version first, then I'll fold the reconciliation into the page.

**7ac91dd4f — yes, it fixes the hazard.** Unknown top-level blocks are tolerated and round-tripped through `ModifyUserSettings`; an unknown key *inside* `global` still fails closed; a `null` global is tolerated; test covers all three. Since no released binary ever had the strict loader, there's no compat debt. Two nits, neither blocking:
- `MarshalJSON` is on the pointer receiver, so `json.Marshal(UserSettings{...})` by value would silently drop `extra`. `persistUserSettings` passes a pointer so it's fine today — a value receiver (or a test) closes the footgun.
- The known-block set is a single hardcoded `"global"`. The next security-bearing block (`redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command`) needs the same strictness, so a small `map[key]decodeFn` registry now saves a copy-paste later.

**The other proposal** (pjbgf's, written on `origin/paulo-goroot` — 5 commits adding `gitdir`/`entiredir`/`worktreedir` as `os.Root` anchors) is largely complementary to mine; it's the lifecycle/scope axis, mine is the trust axis. Where they meet:

- **Adopt theirs for layout**: two roots + buckets + R1–R6, and their `entiredir`/`gitdir` packages *are* my proposed `safefile` — drop my name, extend theirs. R6 (split the on-disk vs in-tree `EntireMetadataDir` constant) is a prerequisite I missed.
- **Adopt mine for trust**: exec-bearing keys (OPF `command`) only from `~/.config/entire/settings.json`. Their `<common>/entire/config/settings.local.json` fixes the per-worktree duplication for everything else, and with the file out of the worktree the index/HEAD probe dies in both plans.
- **One real conflict**: per-worktree runtime. #2030 uses `<common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/`; they use `<git-dir>/entire/` (git's own `.git/worktrees/<name>/`). Theirs is better — git prunes it on `worktree remove`, no hash key — so #2030 should switch.
- **One bug in their R4**: "`run/` is deletable at any moment, including mid-session" is unsafe for lock files — flock/LockFileEx are held on the inode/handle, so deleting a held `.lock` lets a second process lock a fresh file and both proceed. `entire clean` must not sweep `run/` blind.
- **Their `preferences.json` stays in `config/`** but contains a 1-hour trails cache — violates their own bucket rule; at minimum that half moves to `cache/`.
- **Windows is absent** from theirs; my checklist applies, and `.git/worktrees/<name>/entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/…` is deeper than today, so long paths get worse.
- Minor: they count eleven git-dir entries; `entire-search` on main makes it twelve.

input.new_string:
This is one half of a pair

It was written before reading “Where the Entire CLI puts its files” (pjbgf, on origin/paulo-goroot). That document is the layout axis — two git roots, lifecycle buckets, rules R1–R6; this one is the trust axis — who owns each file and what may be honored from it. They are mostly complementary; the reconciliation below says exactly where they meet, where they conflict, and which one should give.

The compat hazard flagged below is already fixed on #2030

Commit 7ac91dd4f (per-block strictness for the user settings file) tolerates and round-trips unknown top-level blocks while keeping global strict. Two nits remain: MarshalJSON is on the pointer receiver, so a by-value marshal silently drops the preserved blocks; and the known-block set is a single hardcoded key, so the next security-bearing block needs a small registry rather than a second copy of the loop.

Reconciliation with “Where the Entire CLI puts its files”

Three axes, not one: root (worktree · git-dir · git-common-dir · user home) answers who else can see it; bucket (config · state · cache · run · logs · tmp) answers may I delete it; tier (user · clone · worktree · remote) answers who could have written it. Their R1 — everything under .entire/ is committed — is what makes the trust axis clean: the whole worktree root becomes one trust class.

Take from theirs

  • The layout and rules R1–R6 as written. Two rev-parse roots, six buckets, one path package, a test that forbids joins elsewhere.
  • R6 first. Split the on-disk paths.EntireMetadataDir from the in-tree path on entire/checkpoints/v1. This document missed it; nothing else can move safely before it lands.
  • gitdir / entiredir / worktreedir are the primitives. They already anchor every os.Root on a trusted base and refuse what Root only confined. The safefile package proposed below should not exist as a separate name — ReadOwned becomes a fourth anchor for the user tier, and ValidateID lives beside entiredir.Name.
  • settings.local.json → <common>/entire/config/. Per clone instead of per worktree fixes the duplication for every local key, not just the exec-bearing ones, and kills the index probe in both plans.
  • Per-worktree runtime under <git-dir>/entire/, not <common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/. This is the one direct collision between the two in-flight branches: #2030's RepoPolicy.RuntimeRoot() builds the hash form. Git's own .git/worktrees/<name>/ is removed by git worktree remove/prune, needs no worktreeid key, and collapses to the common dir for the main worktree. #2030 should switch.

Keep from this one

  • Exec-bearing keys are honored only from ~/.config/entire/settings.json. A git directory is owner-controlled in practice but not by construction — --shared/--reference alternates, a shared bare repo on NFS, a tarball that ships .git. The user's home is the only root that is theirs by definition, so it is the only place a string that becomes argv[0] may come from. Their config/settings.local.json carries everything else.
  • The user tier is in scope. Their document declares ~/.config/entire “already well-formed” and out of scope; the OPF move, per-repo preferences and the trails cache all land there or in ~/.cache. LoadUserSettings strict-decodes the whole file and any unknown key turns the global tier off machine-wide (by design, fail closed). See schema.

name: fs-trust-tiers-investigation
description: "2026-08-28 investigation into a per-user Entire config home (OPF first), dissolving .git/entire/preferences.json, and a filesystem trust-tier convention; where the prior art lives"

On 2026-08-28 Peyton asked for a design investigation: a `~/.config/entire` settings home (so OPF `command` etc. stop needing a per-worktree `.entire/settings.local.json`), a home for the contents of `.git/entire/preferences.json` (review prefs + trails enablement cache grab bag), and a filesystem convention aligned to trust boundaries (os.Root, safer primitives) to stop per-vector CVE fixes (GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf repo-settings ACE; CVE-2026-57208 SessionID traversal).

Key prior art to build on, not beside:
- PR #2030 (`feat/global-trust`, Peyton's; freshest head `fix/global-takeover-migration`) already adds `~/.config/entire/settings.json` with a `global` block, `repopolicy.LoadUserSettings/ModifyUserSettings`, `userdirs.ResolveConfig()`, `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks`, and `RepoPolicy.RuntimeRoot()` → `<git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/`.
- PR #2154/#2156 (pjbgf, merged 2026-08-28): `.entire` must be a real dir, no symlinked children, `readConfined` refuses symlinks. PR #2163: `userdirs.EnsurePrivateDir` (0700).
- Hazard flagged: #2030 strict-decodes the whole user file, so adding keys breaks older binaries on the same machine — needs per-block decoding first.

Proposal artifact: "Entire Filesystem Trust Tiers" (published from this session). Recommended first PR: user-tier loader in `settings`, `safefile` package (ReadOwned/ReadConfined/WriteAtomic), `os.UserHomeDir` lint fence, OPF `command` honored from the user file.

**Why:** Several branches touch the same files; a new design that ignores #2030 would collide with it.
**How to apply:** When continuing this work, read `fix/global-takeover-migration` first and check whether #2030 has merged. See [[repo-checkout-in-icloud-broken]].

Fair. Here's the plan, stripped to what's actually left to do given #2030 already owns the user file and pjbgf's branch already owns the layout.

## What's already decided (don't re-litigate)

- User settings file = `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (#2030). Per-block strict (7ac91dd4f).
- Layout = two rev-parse roots + buckets, R1–R6 (pjbgf). `gitdir`/`entiredir`/`worktreedir` are the `os.Root` primitives (`paulo-goroot`).

## The one rule this adds

**Anything Entire will execute is read from `~/.config/entire/settings.json` only.** Not from `.entire/`, not from `.git/`. That's the whole trust contribution; everything else is plumbing.

## Work items

**A. OPF to the user file** (#2030 or a small follow-up)
1. Add a strict `redaction` top-level block: `openai_privacy_filter.{command, timeout_seconds, prompt_default}`. `enabled`/`categories` stay in the team's `.entire/settings.json`.
2. Turn the hardcoded `"global"` in `UnmarshalJSON` into a `map[key]decodeFn` so `redaction` gets the same strictness.
3. `enforceOPFCommandTrust`: user file → accept, no probe. Local file → still works, warns once. Next minor: delete the local path and `classifyLocalSettingsDeep`.
4. Fix the `MarshalJSON` pointer-receiver footgun.

**B. Fix the one conflict between the two branches** (#2030)
- `RepoPolicy.RuntimeRoot()` → `<git-dir>/entire/` instead of `<common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/`. Git prunes it, no hash key needed.

**C. Two corrections to pjbgf's doc** (comments on his proposal, not code)
- R4: `entire clean` must not delete held lock files (inode-held locks → two holders). Locks stay beside data or `clean` try-locks first.
- `preferences.json` is half cache; split trails cache into `cache/`.

**D. `preferences.json`** (after B, own PR)
- Trails cache → `<common>/entire/cache/`. Review prefs → `<common>/entire/config/` (simplest, matches his layout). Skip the per-repo `repos` map in the user file unless someone asks for cross-clone prefs. Delete `ClonePreferences`.

**E. Windows** (fold into whichever PR touches the primitive)
- Rename retry on sharing violation in the atomic writer.
- Absolutize/MSYS-normalize `rev-parse --git-dir` output before joining.
- `ValidateID` rejects reserved device names.
- User tier: resolve-then-open, no `os.Root` (junctions).

## Suggested sequence

R6 (metadata constant split) → A + B on #2030 → pjbgf's bucket moves with the R4 fix → D → E lands opportunistically.

The dropped-from-artifact items: `safefile` package (his packages cover it), per-repo `repos` map (YAGNI for now), moving `sessions/` to a state dir (do it when #1959 lands, not before), Windows config-location debate (stay put).

content.text:
There is, but it's all hardening of the *existing* worktree gate — nothing reads OPF from the user file yet. What #2030 changes in `opf_command_trust.go` (+128 lines):

- **Symlinked `.entire`/`settings.local.json` is never "owned"** for the command.
- **Gitlink/submodule at `.entire`** counts as tracked (a submodule is a real dir that defeats the symlink probe while `--recurse-submodules` delivers its contents).
- **Location gate:** a `command` that resolves inside the worktree (relative-with-separator, or absolute under the root) is rejected regardless of ownership — `exec.ErrDot` only guards `$PATH` lookups.
- **Egress hold skips OPF:** `prePush` returns before OPF when the repo is held pending trust, so untrusted repos never run the binary.

So the local-file + index/HEAD probe design is still the only source of `command` on #2030. Work item A in the plan (strict `redaction` block in the user file, accept without probe, deprecate the local path) is genuinely new — and it's what lets you eventually delete the probe machinery #2030 just made more elaborate. The location gate (#3) should carry over to the user-file path as-is: a `command` pointing inside *any* worktree stays rejected wherever the string came from.

Yes. Here's the full structure, then a PR split, then three decisions I need before cutting a branch.

## Full structure (Paulo's layout + #2030's user file + the trust rule)

```
~/.config/entire/                          USER · owner-trusted · symlinks followed · 0700/0600
├── settings.json          global{} (#2030) · redaction.openai_privacy_filter{command,timeout_seconds,prompt_default} (new, strict)
│                          review_profiles / review_default_profile / investigate / summary_generation (new, tolerant)
├── contexts.json · tokens.json · version_check.json
~/.cache/entire/                           USER · rebuildable
└── repos/<host/owner/repo>/trails.json    ← trails enablement cache (from preferences.json)

<git-common-dir>/entire/                   CLONE · shared by worktrees · os.Root via gitdir
├── config/   settings.local.json (← .entire/) · preferences.json (review prefs only) · checkpoint-sync-remotes.json · redactors/local/
├── state/    sessions/ · investigations/ · review/manifests/ · checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl
├── cache/    redact-cache/ · search/
└── run/      *-spawn throttle markers only  — locks stay beside their data (R4 fix)

<git-dir>/entire/                          CLONE · this worktree · replaces #2030's worktree/<hash>/
├── logs/ · metadata/<session>/ · tmp/

<worktree>/.entire/                        WORKTREE · repo-controlled · os.Root via entiredir · symlinks refused
└── settings.json · runners/ · redactors/*.yaml      (committed only — R1; .gitignore deleted)
```

One rule on top: **`argv[0]` comes from `~/.config/entire/settings.json` or nowhere.** #2030's location gate (command inside any worktree → rejected) carries over unchanged.

## PR split

Everything must stack on `feat/global-trust` — the user-file loader doesn't exist on `main`.

163:### Why `command` is local-only
164-
165-`command` becomes `argv[0]` of a process Entire executes during `git push`, so
166-whoever controls that string controls what runs on the developer's machine.
167-`.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled, which would let an ordinary pull
168-request pair a `command` with a payload committed alongside it — and a JSON
169-settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer. The pre-push prompt is
170-no defense either: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips
171-it, and non-TTY pushes (CI, agent-driven) auto-run.
172-
173-Entire therefore honors `command` only when it is genuinely developer-owned:
174-
175-- it must come from `.entire/settings.local.json`, not `.entire/settings.json`
176-- that file must be **untracked** — absent from both the git index and `HEAD`
177-- that file must not sit inside a **submodule or nested repository** mounted at `.entire` (an index/`HEAD` entry named `.entire`, or an `.entire/.git` on disk) — `git clone --recurse-submodules` delivers such a file exactly like a committed one
178-- the command must **not resolve inside the repository worktree** (no `./…`, no absolute path under the repo root): an executable that ships with the repo is what this rule exists to keep out, so install the binary elsewhere or use a bare `$PATH` name
179-
180-The second check matters because the filename alone proves nothing:
181-`.gitignore` does not apply to a path that is already tracked, so
182-`git add -f .entire/settings.local.json` commits it and a fresh clone
183-materializes it with the committed content.
184-
185-This is enforced for the whole file, not just this setting: a tracked
186-`.entire/settings.local.json` is ignored in its entirety, because it is not
187-local to your clone — it arrives with the repository and would override project
188-settings for everyone. Entire warns on stderr and tells you to run
189-`git rm --cached .entire/settings.local.json`. The load still succeeds using
190-project settings, so a committed file cannot brick the repository.
191-
192-The two checks also differ in depth. The layer check looks at the git index; the
193-`command` check also looks at `HEAD`. A pull request that commits the file puts

=== global-tracking.md settings-file section ===
## The settings file

`~/.config/entire/settings.json` (or `$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json`) is
decoded with **per-block strictness**: the `global` block rejects unknown keys
— an unknown key inside it, or malformed JSON, turns the tier off machine-wide
(fail closed; an older binary must never misread recorded consent) and
`entire doctor` says so — while unknown **top-level** blocks are ignored and
preserved byte-for-byte across writes, so a newer `entire` on the same machine
can add a block without switching the tier off for older binaries. New
features add top-level blocks, not keys inside `global`.

```json
{
  "global": {
    "enabled": true,
    "exclude_paths": ["~/scratch/**"],
    "exclude_paths_exact": ["~"],
    "exclude_origins": ["github.com/acme/private-*"],
    "trust_all": false,
    "trusted_origins": ["github.com/acme/widgets"],
    "trusted_paths": ["/Users/me/code/notes"]
  }
}
```

- `enabled` — both `true` and `false` count as *configured*; an absent block is
  *unconfigured* (zero cost, no user-level hooks).
- `exclude_paths` — `~`-expanded doublestar globs against the worktree root (a
  bare directory pattern excludes its subtree). `exclude_paths_exact` matches
  one root only, no cascade — the way to exclude `$HOME` as a dotfiles repo
  without excluding everything under it. `exclude_origins` — globs against the
  origin URL normalized to `host/owner/repo`. An unusable pattern, or an origin
  that is present but cannot be normalized, deactivates the tier for that repo
  (fail closed).
- `trust_all`, `trusted_origins`, `trusted_paths` — checkpoint-egress consent

=== CLAUDE.md OPF trust bullet line ===
767:- **OPF's `command` is a trust boundary, not a setting**: `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` becomes `argv[0]` of an exec during pre-push, and `.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled — so reading it from the project file would let a pull request execute code on every developer who pushes (the prompt is no defense: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips it, and non-TTY pushes auto-run). `settings.enforceOPFCommandTrust` (`settings/opf_command_trust.go`) honors `command` only from `.entire/settings.local.json`, and only when that file is untracked in **both** the index and `HEAD` — the filename is not the check, because `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path. The probe goes through go-git (`gitrepo.OpenPath`), not the git CLI, and is memoized per process: shelling out cost ~15 subprocesses per hook (`settings.Load` is uncached and runs several times per hook) and would fail verification wherever `git` is off `$PATH` — the GUI-git-client population that most needs an explicit `command`. **Two depths**: the layer check reads the index only, because a PR-delivered file is always in the index of a clone that checks it out, and checkout cannot produce a file absent from the index; the `command` check also reads HEAD. decoded with **per-block strictness**: the `global` block rejects unknown keys

input.old_string:
### Why `command` is local-only

`command` becomes `argv[0]` of a process Entire executes during `git push`, so
whoever controls that string controls what runs on the developer's machine.
`.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled, which would let an ordinary pull
request pair a `command` with a payload committed alongside it — and a JSON
settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer. The pre-push prompt is
no defense either: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips
it, and non-TTY pushes (CI, agent-driven) auto-run.

Entire therefore honors `command` only when it is genuinely developer-owned:

- it must come from `.entire/settings.local.json`, not `.entire/settings.json`
- that file must be **untracked** — absent from both the git index and `HEAD`
input.new_string:
### Why `command` is user-only

`command` becomes `argv[0]` of a process Entire executes during `git push`, so
whoever controls that string controls what runs on the developer's machine.
`.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled, which would let an ordinary pull
request pair a `command` with a payload committed alongside it — and a JSON
settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer. The pre-push prompt is
no defense either: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips
it, and non-TTY pushes (CI, agent-driven) auto-run.

Entire therefore honors `command` only when it is genuinely developer-owned.
The supported location is the **user settings file**,
`~/.config/entire/settings.json`: it lives outside every repository, so no
clone, submodule, or symlink can put content there, and a `command` read from
it needs no further verification — the only remaining check is that the binary
must not resolve inside the repository worktree (below). A user-file `command`
supersedes one in `.entire/settings.local.json`. `timeout_seconds` and
`prompt_default` may be set there too; they apply on top of the project file
and beneath `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the prompt's **Always** (which
writes to the local file) still wins. `enabled` and `categories` are team
policy and are rejected from the user file.

The older location, `.entire/settings.local.json`, is **deprecated** and will
be removed in a future release; each push that relies on it prints a hint. For
now it is still honored, but only when all of the following hold:

- it must come from `.entire/settings.local.json`, not `.entire/settings.json`
- that file must be **untracked** — absent from both the git index and `HEAD`

When a `command` fails these checks it is ignored with a warning in
`.entire/logs/entire.log` and OPF falls back to resolving `opf` on `$PATH`. If
that binary is missing, the pre-push rewrite fails closed rather than pushing
content you believed OPF had scanned. Everything else in the OPF block
(`enabled`, `categories`, `timeout_seconds`, `prompt_default`) is ordinary
configuration and still works from the shared project file.
input.new_string:
When a `command` fails these checks — from either file — it is ignored with a
warning in `.entire/logs/entire.log` and OPF falls back to resolving `opf` on
`$PATH`. If that binary is missing, the pre-push rewrite fails closed rather
than pushing content you believed OPF had scanned. Everything else in the OPF
block (`enabled`, `categories`, `timeout_seconds`, `prompt_default`) is
ordinary configuration and still works from the shared project file.

input.old_string: `settings.enforceOPFCommandTrust` (`settings/opf_command_trust.go`) honors `command` only from `.entire/settings.local.json`, and only when that file is untracked in **both** the index and `HEAD` — the filename is not the check, because `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path.
input.new_string: **The supported home is the user settings file**: `~/.config/entire/settings.json` carries a strict `redaction.openai_privacy_filter` block (`command`, `timeout_seconds`, `prompt_default` — never `enabled`/`categories`, which are team policy and stay in the project file; `repopolicy.UserOPFConfig`). That file is the developer's by construction — no clone, submodule, or symlink can deliver content into it — so `settings.enforceOPFCommandTrust` (`settings/opf_command_trust.go`) takes a `command` from there first and honors it with **no ownership probe** (no index read, no HEAD read), subject only to the location gate below; it supersedes any local-file value and is tagged `OPFCommandSourceUser`. `timeout_seconds`/`prompt_default` from the user file layer *between* the project and local files (`applyUserOPFPreferences`), so the pre-push prompt's "Always" — which writes to the local file — still wins; the user file never creates an OPF block the repository did not configure, and an unreadable user file only skips the overlay (repo-enabled capture must not depend on it). **Deprecated path**: absent a user-file command, `.entire/settings.local.json` is still honored — tagged `OPFCommandSourceLocal`, with a move-it hint printed at each push — but only when that file is untracked in **both** the index and `HEAD` — the filename is not the check, because `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path. Removing the local path removes `classifyLocalSettingsDeep` and the HEAD probe with it.

toolUseResult.oldString:
### Why `command` is local-only

`command` becomes `argv[0]` of a process Entire executes during `git push`, so
whoever controls that string controls what runs on the developer's machine.
`.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled, which would let an ordinary pull
request pair a `command` with a payload committed alongside it — and a JSON
settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer. The pre-push prompt is
no defense either: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips
it, and non-TTY pushes (CI, agent-driven) auto-run.

Entire therefore honors `command` only when it is genuinely developer-owned:

- it must come from `.entire/settings.local.json`, not `.entire/settings.json`
- that file must be **untracked** — absent from both the git index and `HEAD`

### Why `command` is user-only

`command` becomes `argv[0]` of a process Entire executes during `git push`, so
whoever controls that string controls what runs on the developer's machine.
`.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled, which would let an ordinary pull
request pair a `command` with a payload committed alongside it — and a JSON
settings diff does not read as executable to a reviewer. The pre-push prompt is
no defense either: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips
it, and non-TTY pushes (CI, agent-driven) auto-run.

Entire therefore honors `command` only when it is genuinely developer-owned.
The supported location is the **user settings file**,
`~/.config/entire/settings.json`: it lives outside every repository, so no
clone, submodule, or symlink can put content there, and a `command` read from
it needs no further verification — the only remaining check is that the binary
must not resolve inside the repository worktree (below). A user-file `command`
supersedes one in `.entire/settings.local.json`. `timeout_seconds` and
`prompt_default` may be set there too; they apply on top of the project file
and beneath `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the prompt's **Always** (which
writes to the local file) still wins. `enabled` and `categories` are team
policy and are rejected from the user file.

The older location, `.entire/settings.local.json`, is **deprecated** and will
be removed in a future release; each push that relies on it prints a hint. For
now it is still honored, but only when all of the following hold:

- it must come from `.entire/settings.local.json`, not `.entire/settings.json`
- that file must be **untracked** — absent from both the git index and `HEAD`

lines: - **Checkpoint egress trust gate** - `settings.CheckpointEgressAllowed(ctx)` is the single predicate for whether checkpoint data may leave the machine: while the user-global tier is off or unconfigured, an active repo syncs as before; once `global.enabled` is true every active repo — repo-enabled or globally tracked — needs `global.trust_all`, a trusted key for the **elected checkpoint sync remote** (`trusted_origins` holds that remote's normalized `host/owner/repo` URLs — origin only by default; a `checkpoint_push_remote`, captured election, or pending capture on the current push re-keys it, so a re-election re-asks), or a trusted path when that remote has no normalizable URL. `repopolicy.ResolveSyncRemote` is the seam: strategy installs the election into it at init (`strategy/trust_sync_remote.go`), the same way settings installs `LocalSettingsTrusted`. `entire enable` records that trust itself, the three-option pre-push prompt ("Yes — trust this repo / Not now — re-ask next push / Always — trust every repo (trust_all)") records it interactively, and `entire trust [--revoke] [--remote <name>]` manages it (`--remote` records consent for a remote a held push is about to capture — the election persists only on delivery, so plain `trust` would key the still-elected remote); errors fail closed. Both egress entry points are gated — `ManualCommitStrategy.prePush` (early return beside the single-remote gate, above both backend branches, so held repos never run OPF) and `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs`. A hold never blocks the user's own push: the branch pushes, checkpoint data stays local (refs-backend refs stay queued) with one stderr explanation, and the first trusted push drains the backlog. Activation, runtime layout, user-level hooks, and lazy setup are documented in `docs/architecture/global-tracking.md`.

- **Scanner engine selection is a settings-only, fail-closed choice**: `redaction.betterleaks.enabled` (default `true`) and `redaction.goredact.enabled` (default `false`) pick which pattern-matching engine(s) feed layer 2 of `detectAllLayers` (`redact.ConfigureScanners`, `redact/scanners.go`). Both keys are honored from committed `.entire/settings.json` only — a `settings.local.json` copy is ignored with a logged warning, because the choice affects everyone who reads the repo's checkpoints, not just the developer who set it. `validateScannerSettings` fails settings load with `settings.ErrScannerConfig` when both engines are disabled. If goredact is the sole enabled engine and its scan fails at runtime, `redact.ErrScannerDegraded` propagates out of `JSONLBytes`/`JSONLBytesWithPrivacyFilter`; every checkpoint-write call site (`checkpoint/ephemeral.go`, `checkpoint/persistent.go`, `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`) must `errors.Is` for it and fail the write rather than fall back to under-scanned content. See `docs/security-and-privacy.md` for user-facing details.

- **OPF (OpenAI Privacy Filter) runs at pre-push, not post-commit**: when `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.enabled` is true, the PrePush hook re-redacts unpushed commits with the OPF 9th layer, builds new commits carrying an `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` trailer, and updates the local refs before pushing. Per-commit condensation stays on the fast 8-layer pipeline. **Both backends are covered, by two rewrites sharing one policy**: `manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go` walks unpushed `entire/checkpoints/v1` commits bounded by the remote tip and CAS-updates the branch; `manual_commit_opf_refs.go` walks the push queue and, per queued ref, rewrites every unpushed commit — stopping at the first commit already carrying the trailer, which makes the trailer its own watermark (steady state stops at the tip's parent) and is bounded by the shared `BootstrapTooLargeError` cap for repos that enable OPF late. Blob policy, byte caps, the single batched shell-out, and the error taxonomy are shared; only discovery and ref update differ. **Fail-closed differs by backend on purpose**: git-branch aborts the user's push, while git-refs withholds the (separately-pushed) checkpoint refs and leaves them queued, so nothing under-redacted ships without blocking the user's own push. See `docs/security-and-privacy.md` for the full flow, including divergence detection, bootstrap caps, and CAS-on-conflict semantics.

-- **OPF's `command` is a trust boundary, not a setting**: `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` becomes `argv[0]` of an exec during pre-push, and `.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled — so reading it from the project file would let a pull request execute code on every developer who pushes (the prompt is no defense: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips it, and non-TTY pushes auto-run). `settings.enforceOPFCommandTrust` (`settings/opf_command_trust.go`) honors `command` only from `.entire/settings.local.json`, and only when that file is untracked in **both** the index and `HEAD` — the filename is not the check, because `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path. The probe goes through go-git (`gitrepo.OpenPath`), not the git CLI, and is memoized per process: shelling out cost ~15 subprocesses per hook (`settings.Load` is uncached and runs several times per hook) and would fail verification wherever `git` is off `$PATH` — the GUI-git-client population that most needs an explicit `command`. **Two depths**: the layer check reads the index only, because a PR-delivered file is always in the index of a clone that checks it out, and checkout cannot produce a file absent from the index; the `command` check also reads HEAD. That split matters because HEAD is the expensive half — measured 8.3ms → 2.5ms per hook process in this repo, and 39ms → 11ms on reftable, where `gitrepo` routes reference reads back through the git CLI. The cost falls on everyone with a `settings.local.json`, not just OPF users, so keep it off the HEAD path. Rejection is a downgrade to the documented `$PATH` default plus a warning, never a hard error; verification failure (no repo, git missing) counts as untrusted. **Versioned means more than the file's own path**: an index or HEAD entry *named* `.entire` (a gitlink/submodule, or a blob standing where the directory should be) and an `.entire/.git` on disk all count as tracked — a submodule mounted at `.entire` is a real directory that defeats the symlink probe while `git clone --recurse-submodules` delivers its contents. **Location is a second gate**: a `command` that resolves inside the worktree (relative with a separator, or absolute under the root) is rejected regardless of ownership, because `exec.ErrDot` only guards `$PATH` lookups and a repo-delivered binary is exactly what the gate exists to block. Do not add other exec-bearing fields to the project settings file without the same gate.

input.content:
Stacked on #2030 (`feat/global-trust`). First slice of the filesystem trust-tier work: the one rule this adds is **anything Entire will execute is read from `~/.config/entire/settings.json`, or nowhere.**

## What

**OPF `command` moves to the user settings file.** `~/.config/entire/settings.json` gains a strict `redaction` block:

```json
{
  "redaction": {
    "openai_privacy_filter": { "command": "/opt/opf/bin/opf", "timeout_seconds": 120, "prompt_default": "ask" }
  }
}
```

- `command` from the user file is honored with **no ownership probe** — no git index read, no HEAD read — because that file is the developer's by construction: no clone, submodule, or symlink can deliver content into it. It supersedes a local-file command. The "command resolves inside the worktree" location gate from #2030 still applies to it.
- `timeout_seconds` / `prompt_default` layer **between** the project file and `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the pre-push prompt's "Always" (which writes to the local file) still wins.
- `enabled` / `categories` are team policy and stay in the repo's `.entire/settings.json`; they are unknown keys in the user file and fail closed. The user file never creates an OPF block the repo did not configure.
- An unreadable user file skips the overlay (debug log) rather than failing `settings.Load` — repo-enabled capture must not depend on it, same rule `repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` applies.
- `.entire/settings.local.json` still works when untracked (existing probe), tagged `OPFCommandSourceLocal`; pre-push prints a move-it hint. Slated for removal next minor, which deletes `classifyLocalSettingsDeep` and the HEAD probe.

**Per-block decoder becomes a registry.** `repopolicy.userSettingsBlocks` maps `global` and `redaction` to strict decoders; unknown top-level blocks are still preserved (7ac91dd4f). Adding a block is a field + a table entry. `MarshalJSON` moves to a value receiver so `json.Marshal(UserSettings{})` by value can no longer silently drop preserved blocks.

**Windows hygiene, in the primitives:**
- `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic` retries the rename on `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` / `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION` / `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` with ~155 ms of backoff (a concurrent hook, an editor, or Defender holding the destination — the #455 failure shape). No-op on POSIX.
- Every ID validator (`validation.Validate{Session,ToolUse,Agent,AgentSession}ID`) rejects Windows reserved device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`, `con.txt`, `NUL.`, …) on every platform — IDs travel in checkpoint metadata and are restored on whatever machine pulls them; `os.Root` refuses these but a plain `filepath.Join` does not.

## Why this shape

Today the exec-bearing setting lives in repository-controlled space, so the loader has to *prove* on every load that the file is not tracked — the index probe on every `settings.Load`, plus a HEAD read whenever the command is set. A file under `~/.config` needs no such proof. This is the trust half of the layout proposal in "Where the Entire CLI puts its files"; the two are reconciled in the design page linked in the thread.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- `RuntimeRoot()` → `<git-dir>/entire/` instead of `<common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/`
- dissolving `.git/entire/preferences.json` (trails cache → `~/.cache`, review prefs → user file)
- `entire clean` try-locking before removing `.lock` files
- removing the local-file OPF path

## Validation

`mise run check`: fmt clean, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, unit + integration + Vogon canary (output in thread). `GOOS=windows go build ./...` and `go vet` on the new files pass. New tests: `TestLoadUserSettings_RedactionBlock`, `TestLoadUserSettings_NullRedactionBlockIsUnset`, `TestUserSettings_MarshalByValuePreservesEveryBlock`, `TestOPFCommandTrust_UserFile*` (honored / wins over tracked local / wins over untracked local / inside-worktree rejected), `TestOPFCommandTrust_LocalCommandIsTaggedAsDeprecatedSource`, `TestOPFUserSettings_*` (does not enable OPF / layering / malformed user file skipped), `TestValidators_RejectWindowsReservedDeviceNames`, `TestRetryRename_*`. No real-agent E2E run.

Stacked on #2030 (`feat/global-trust`). First slice of the filesystem trust-tier work: the one rule this adds is **anything Entire will execute is read from `~/.config/entire/settings.json`, or nowhere.**

## What

**OPF `command` moves to the user settings file.** `~/.config/entire/settings.json` gains a strict `redaction` block:

```json
{
  "redaction": {
    "openai_privacy_filter": { "command": "/opt/opf/bin/opf", "timeout_seconds": 120, "prompt_default": "ask" }
  }
}
```

- `command` from the user file is honored with **no ownership probe** — no git index read, no HEAD read — because that file is the developer's by construction: no clone, submodule, or symlink can deliver content into it. It supersedes a local-file command. The "command resolves inside the worktree" location gate from #2030 still applies to it.
- `timeout_seconds` / `prompt_default` layer **between** the project file and `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the pre-push prompt's "Always" (which writes to the local file) still wins.
- `enabled` / `categories` are team policy and stay in the repo's `.entire/settings.json`; they are unknown keys in the user file and fail closed. The user file never creates an OPF block the repo did not configure.
- An unreadable user file skips the overlay (debug log) rather than failing `settings.Load` — repo-enabled capture must not depend on it, same rule `repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` applies.
- `.entire/settings.local.json` still works when untracked (existing probe), tagged `OPFCommandSourceLocal`; pre-push prints a move-it hint. Slated for removal next minor, which deletes `classifyLocalSettingsDeep` and the HEAD probe.

**Per-block decoder becomes a registry.** `repopolicy.userSettingsBlocks` maps `global` and `redaction` to strict decoders; unknown top-level blocks are still preserved (7ac91dd4f). Adding a block is a field + a table entry. `MarshalJSON` moves to a value receiver so `json.Marshal(UserSettings{})` by value can no longer silently drop preserved blocks.

**Windows hygiene, in the primitives:**
- `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic` retries the rename on `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` / `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION` / `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` with ~155 ms of backoff (a concurrent hook, an editor, or Defender holding the destination — the #455 failure shape). No-op on POSIX.
- Every ID validator (`validation.Validate{Session,ToolUse,Agent,AgentSession}ID`) rejects Windows reserved device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`, `con.txt`, `NUL.`, …) on every platform — IDs travel in checkpoint metadata and are restored on whatever machine pulls them; `os.Root` refuses these but a plain `filepath.Join` does not.

## Why this shape

Today the exec-bearing setting lives in repository-controlled space, so the loader has to *prove* on every load that the file is not tracked — the index probe on every `settings.Load`, plus a HEAD read whenever the command is set. A file under `~/.config` needs no such proof. This is the trust half of the layout proposal in "Where the Entire CLI puts its files"; the two are reconciled in the design page linked in the thread.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- `RuntimeRoot()` → `<git-dir>/entire/` instead of `<common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/`
- dissolving `.git/entire/preferences.json` (trails cache → `~/.cache`, review prefs → user file)
- `entire clean` try-locking before removing `.lock` files
- removing the local-file OPF path

Stacked on #2030 (`feat/global-trust`). First slice of the filesystem trust-tier work: the one rule this adds is **anything Entire will execute is read from `~/.config/entire/settings.json`, or nowhere.**

## What

**OPF `command` moves to the user settings file.** `~/.config/entire/settings.json` gains a strict `redaction` block:

```json
{
  "redaction": {
    "openai_privacy_filter": { "command": "/opt/opf/bin/opf", "timeout_seconds": 120, "prompt_default": "ask" }
  }
}
```

- `command` from the user file is honored with **no ownership probe** — no git index read, no HEAD read — because that file is the developer's by construction: no clone, submodule, or symlink can deliver content into it. It supersedes a local-file command. The "command resolves inside the worktree" location gate from #2030 still applies to it.
- `timeout_seconds` / `prompt_default` layer **between** the project file and `.entire/settings.local.json`: applied after the local merge (so a local file that *creates* the OPF block still gets them) but yielding to any key the local file set explicitly, so the pre-push prompt's "Always" (which writes to the local file) still wins. `0`/`""` mean "not set here".
- `enabled` / `categories` are team policy and stay in the repo's `.entire/settings.json`; they are unknown keys in the user file and fail closed. The user file never creates an OPF block the repo did not configure.
- An unreadable user file skips the overlay (debug log) rather than failing `settings.Load` — repo-enabled capture must not depend on it, same rule `repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` applies.
- `.entire/settings.local.json` still works when untracked (existing probe), tagged `OPFCommandSourceLocal`; pre-push prints a move-it hint. Slated for removal next minor, which deletes `classifyLocalSettingsDeep` and the HEAD probe.

**Per-block decoder becomes a registry.** `repopolicy.userSettingsBlocks` maps `global` and `redaction` to strict decoders; unknown top-level blocks are still preserved (7ac91dd4f). Adding a block is a field + a table entry. `MarshalJSON` moves to a value receiver so `json.Marshal(UserSettings{})` by value can no longer silently drop preserved blocks.

**Windows hygiene, in the primitives:**
- `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic` retries the rename on `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` / `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION` / `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` with ~155 ms of backoff (a concurrent hook, an editor, or Defender holding the destination — the #455 failure shape). No-op on POSIX.
- Every ID validator (`validation.Validate{Session,ToolUse,Agent,AgentSession}ID`) rejects Windows reserved device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`, `con.txt`, `NUL.`, …) on every platform — IDs travel in checkpoint metadata and are restored on whatever machine pulls them; `os.Root` refuses these but a plain `filepath.Join` does not.

## Why this shape

Today the exec-bearing setting lives in repository-controlled space, so the loader has to *prove* on every load that the file is not tracked — the index probe on every `settings.Load`, plus a HEAD read whenever the command is set. A file under `~/.config` needs no such proof. This is the trust half of the layout proposal in "Where the Entire CLI puts its files"; the two are reconciled in the design page linked in the thread.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- `RuntimeRoot()` → `<git-dir>/entire/` instead of `<common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/`
- dissolving `.git/entire/preferences.json` (trails cache → `~/.cache`, review prefs → user file)
- `entire clean` try-locking before removing `.lock` files
- removing the local-file OPF path
